title: The Forgotten Garden
premise: Ines Marchetti has spent his life as the invisible keeper of the Ledgerhouse, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled memories, borrowed years, names that never existed. When a dying cartographer presses a map of Vessany, a country erased from every record forty years ago, into his hands, Ines learns he was born there and smuggled out as an infant, and that the gate he keeps is the last door back. Hunted by the guild's collectors and shadowed by a woman who remembers Vessany better than she should, Ines must reconstruct his stolen childhood from the ledgers themselves and reopen the gate before it seals forever at the winter solstice. He finds the door, but crossing it means choosing between the identity he was given and the one that was taken; in the end he rewrites the ledger itself, restoring Vessany to memory while remaining its keeper on both sides of the gate.
about_author: Orsen Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed heirlooms in a coastal customs house, where every object seemed to be waiting for someone. The Forgotten Garden is their second novel, following the quietly acclaimed novella Salt for the Dead.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unopened Doors
chapters.summary: Ines Marchetti's POV. A night of routine inventory at the Ledgerhouse establishes his meticulous invisibility: he catalogs impossible goods but never touches them. A collector's visit reminds him the guild watches its keepers. Emotional beat: the comfort—and suffocation—of a life built to leave no trace.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Third Bell
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A bleeding man collapses against the guild's outer gate, pressing a folded map into Ines's hands and whispering 'Vessany' before dying. Ines hides the body and the map, breaking guild law for the first time. Emotional beat: fear curdling into a strange, unwelcome thrill.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Do Not Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Searching the archives for 'Vessany,' Ines finds every page razored out—except one shipping manifest bearing his own surname. He realizes someone erased a country deliberately. Emotional beat: the first crack in his belief that records tell the truth.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: Maren Oduya's POV. Maren, a memory-broker who sells other people's pasts, recognizes the dead cartographer's coat when collectors come asking questions. She lies to them smoothly, then goes looking for whoever took the map. Emotional beat: her loneliness disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Collectors at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Guild enforcers arrive to audit the gate, led by the courteous, terrifying Collector Vane. Ines performs innocence while the map burns against his chest like a coal. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into performance—he discovers he can lie well.

chapters.title: The Map That Folds Wrong
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Alone, Ines unfolds the map and finds it shows streets that rearrange when viewed twice—the geography of a place that resists being remembered. A hidden inscription names a garden. Emotional beat: wonder edged with grief for something he cannot recall.

chapters.title: Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren traces the cartographer's last deals and learns he bought a memory of a garden with everything he had, then tried to give it back. She realizes the trade was never finished. Emotional beat: pity for a client, and the ache of memories that belong to no one.

chapters.title: An Audit of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vane returns with questions about the dead man, watching Ines too closely. Ines survives by volunteering a half-truth, but Vane leaves a mark on the door—a sign Ines's grandmother once drew. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing his past is legible to strangers.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Digging through his few inherited possessions, Ines matches the symbol to letters written in a script no living language uses. His grandmother came from somewhere erased. Emotional beat: anger at the silence she kept, softening into longing.

chapters.title: A Trade in the Fishmarket
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren corners Ines in the fishmarket and offers a partnership: her access to brokered memories for his map. He refuses; she tells him his real name anyway—Inesio Marchetti of Vessany. Emotional beat: the shock of hearing yourself named by a stranger.

chapters.title: The Gatekeeper's Oath
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Flashback chapter: young Ines swearing the keeper's oath—to open for none, remember for all. Now each clause reads differently. He begins copying the mutilated ledgers in secret. Emotional beat: an oath turning from shield into cage.

chapters.title: Memories Not for Sale
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren opens her private vault of memories she refuses to sell, including fragments of Vessany she cannot explain owning. One fragment shows a woman handing a baby over a wall. Emotional beat: dread dawning that her own past may be stolen goods.

chapters.title: Vane's Invitation
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vane offers Ines promotion—chief keeper—in exchange for the map, claiming the guild destroyed Vessany to contain a plague of remembering. The offer is generous, which makes it monstrous. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of safety.

chapters.title: The Garden in the Bottle
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren sells Ines a bottled memory at ruinous cost: a garden where children memorize the country so it cannot be fully erased. Inside it, Ines hears his mother's voice. Emotional beat: grief arriving decades late, all at once.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Erased
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the manifest, Ines finds a hidden annex: a ledger of everyone smuggled out of Vessany, forty-one children, himself listed fourth. Someone inside the guild wrote it. Emotional beat: fury transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Margins
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren identifies the annex's handwriting as belonging to the guild's founder—meaning the erasure had a dissenter at its heart. Collectors raid her shop; she escapes with one memory-vial and nothing else. Emotional beat: loss burning away her caution.

chapters.title: On the Run Together
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ines shelters Maren in the Ledgerhouse's blind corridors. They compare fragments—her memories, his documents—and assemble the shape of the conspiracy. Emotional beat: two guarded people discovering that trust can be practical before it is tender.

chapters.title: The Solstice Clause
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Deciphering the gate's charter, Ines learns it opens onto Vessany only at winter solstice—and this year is the last time before the charter expires forever. Eleven days remain. Emotional beat: a countdown beginning, cold and clean.

chapters.title: What Vane Wants
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane, revealed as a child of Vessany who chose the guild, hunts the map not to destroy it but to keep the gate shut—believing the country's return would unravel the peace built on forgetting. Emotional beat: conviction that looks, uncomfortably, like love.

chapters.title: The Forty-First Child
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren decodes her inexplicable memories: she is the forty-first child, the one the ledger lists without a destination. Her past and Ines's were split deliberately. Emotional beat: identity arriving like a wound finally cleaned.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A junior keeper Ines trusted reports the annex to Vane. Ines barely escapes with the map and ledger as the archive burns behind him. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the liberating clarity of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Doors Within Doors
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Fugitives now, Ines and Maren follow the map's shifting streets through the city's forgotten layers—cellars older than the guild, roads that remember Vessany's names. Emotional beat: exhaustion shot through with awe.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Grave
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They find the dying stranger's burial cache: his journal confessing he was the guild's chief eraser, spending his last years trying to undo his work. He left instructions and an apology. Emotional beat: the possibility that complicity can be answered.

chapters.title: Vane's Trap
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane captures Maren, offering her memories back piece by piece in exchange for Ines's location. She sells him a false trail using a forged memory-vial. Emotional beat: cunning as self-rescue; the broker finally brokering her own freedom.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The journal warns that opening the gate requires a keeper to surrender a memory of equal weight to what returns. Ines begins choosing which memory to pay. Emotional beat: quiet horror at pricing his own life.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Customs House
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Vane's collectors corner them at the old customs house; Maren's forged trail buys hours, not safety. Ines uses guild protocols against the guild, sealing routes behind them. Emotional beat: the hunted becoming, briefly, the hunters.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Waiting out the search, Maren and Ines trade true stories at last—her sold childhood, his chosen invisibility. She admits she followed him for the map first. Emotional beat: honesty as intimacy; forgiveness offered without being asked.

chapters.title: The Founder's Vault
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The journal leads to the founder's sealed vault beneath the Ledgerhouse: the original charter, the erasure order, and a letter naming Vane's family among the erased. Emotional beat: understanding the enemy without excusing him.

chapters.title: Vane's Grief
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Confronted with proof his own parents were from Vessany, Vane wavers—then hardens, insisting the erasure spared them pain. He moves to destroy the gate entirely. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into certainty.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Preparations: Maren brokers alliances with memory-thieves and exiled keepers; Ines restores the razored pages from copies scattered across forty years of ledgers. Emotional beat: a resistance assembling from paper and stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines presents the annex ledger to the guild's council, splitting them—some keepers defect, others call it heresy. Vane forces a vote: seal the gate or open it. Emotional beat: the lonely courage of speaking first.

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane wins the vote and orders the gate bricked. Watching the masons work, he permits himself one moment of doubt. Emotional beat: victory experienced as entombment.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Right
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines invokes an ancient clause only a sworn keeper can use: the right of personal passage, which no vote can revoke. He will open the door alone, from the inside. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Breaking the Wall
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On solstice eve, defected keepers and Maren fight through the guild to reach the gate while Ines works the mechanism from within. Vane confronts them in the final corridor. Emotional beat: chaos held together by sheer will.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Climax. Ines opens the gate onto a twilight Vessany—half-real, sustained only by remembered fragments. Vane arrives; Ines offers him the choice his parents never got. Vane stands down, weeping. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from sorrow.

chapters.title: The Payment
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The gate demands its price. Ines surrenders his memory of the Ledgerhouse—every year of careful invisibility—and steps through whole but hollowed toward his own history. Emotional beat: loss accepted as the cost of becoming.

chapters.title: Vessany, Winter Morning
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren crosses after him into a country rebuilding itself from forty-one returned children's memories. She finds Ines staring at a garden he doesn't recognize but weeps at anyway. Emotional beat: homecoming as recognition without recollection.

chapters.title: New Ledgers
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Weeks later: Vessany writes itself back into the world as its people remember aloud. Maren becomes the broker of returned memories; Vane sends, anonymously, the razored pages he secretly preserved. Emotional beat: repair as collective labor.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Both Sides
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Epilogue. Ines rebuilds the gatehouse on the Vessany side and takes a new oath: open for the lost, remember for all. He keeps a small ledger of names returning through the door—including, one spring day, visitors from the city that forgot. Emotional beat: belonging achieved not as recovery but as choice.
